chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Abdullah, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far, from Ayoub ibn Nuh who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) the third that a group of people asked me about the Fitra, and they ask me to carry its price to you; and this man had been sent to you last year, and he asked me to ask you, but I forgot that, and I have sent to you this year on behalf of each head from my dependents, a dirham, based on the value of nine Rats per dirham. So what is your view, may Allah be my ransom for you, regarding that?

So he (peace be upon him) wrote: 'The Fitra, questions about it have become numerous, and I dislike everything that leads to publicity. Therefore, cease mentioning it, and collect from those who pay it, and withhold from those who do not pay it.'

key_terms.أَرْطَال: Rats, a traditional unit of weight for food measurement
key_terms.الشُّهْرَة: Publicity or fame, here referring to the notoriety of the specific ruling
key_terms.الْفِطْرَة: Zakat al-Fitr, the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan
key_terms.الْقِيمَة: The monetary value or equivalent price

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on paying Zakat al-Fitr in cash according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al--Hasan al-Thani (AS) illustrates the principle of 'satr' (concealment) in Shia jurisprudence, where the Imam discouraged publicizing specific monetary valuations of Zakat al-Fitr to prevent the ritual from becoming a matter of public fame or commercialization. While the obligation to pay remains binding on all dependents, the instruction to 'collect from those who pay and withhold from those who do not' emphasizes the individual's personal responsibility and the Imam's strategic management of religious practice to maintain its spiritual dignity.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Abdullah, from Abdullah Bin Ja’far, from Ayoub Bin Nuh who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> the 3<sup>rd</sup> that a group of people asked me about the Fitra, and are asking me that carry over its price to you<sup>asws</sup>; and I had sent a man to you<sup>asws</sup> last year, and he had asked me to ask you<sup>asws</sup>, but I forgot that, and I have sent to you, on behalf of each head from my dependents, by dirhams upon the price of nine Ratls (a unit of measurement), by Dirhams. So, can I have your<sup>asws</sup> view with regards to that? May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Make me to be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>’.

So he<sup>asws</sup> wrote: ‘The Fitra, the questions have become numerous about it, and I<sup>asws</sup> dislike everything that invites to the publicity. Therefore, cut off the mention of that, and take possession from the ones who hand it over and withhold from the ones who do not hand over’.
en.sarwar: 24. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Ja’far from Ayyub ibn Nuh who has said

the following: “I once wrote to abu al-Hassan, the third, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, that a (certain) people have asked me about al-Fitrah. They ask if they can bring its price to you. In the year before, this man had delivered to you. He had asked me to ask you but I had forgotten about it. This year I have sent you for every one of my dependents one dirham as price of nine Artal for one dirham. Grant us your decision, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.

He (the Imam) wrote to me, ‘Questions about al- Fitrah have become so many and I dislike whatever leads to popularity (unnecessary propagation). Cut down its mention, accept from those who have given, and abstain from those who have not paid.’”
